newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo 1996 wheat output at 25 year low - Institute.
newsitem.headline: Yugo 1996 wheat output at 25 year low - Institute.

text.p: Yugoslavia's 1996 wheat harvest fell to 1.5 million tonnes, half last year's level and the lowest for 25 years, the Institute for Market Research (IZIT) said on Friday.
IZIT based its report on the latest preliminary data obtained from the Federal Statistics Office.
The report said the 1996 harvest also showed that average yields, at 2.6 tonnes per hectare compared to a normal average of 3.5 tonnes, were the lowest for a quarter-century.
The harvest was below even the most pessimistic forecast, which was for about 1.8 million tonnes. Last year's harvest was 2.95 million tonnes, and the record was 4.1 million in 1991.
According to IZIT, the province of Vojvodina -- the bread-basket of Yugoslavia -- produced 834,000 tonnes, while 675,000 tonnes were collected from the rest of Serbia.
The Belgrade-based institute said wheat would be sown this autumn on 850,000 hectares -- 270,000 ha more than last year.
The IZIT report also forecast that the maize crop, which has yet to be harvested, would be 4.956 million tonnes, 15 percent less than in 1995. The total area under maize was 1.442 million hectares.
Wheat and maize are major export earners for Yugoslavia, generating about 12 percent of its total export income which stood at $1.101 billion for the first eight months.
The sugar beet crop was seen jumping by 37 percent to 2.32 million tonnes.
According to official statistics, sunflower production is expected to grow 38 percent to 408,000 tonnes, while soybeans could rise 33 percent to 143,000 tonnes.
But IZIT experts cast some doubt over those forecasts and expected oilseeds production estimates to be revised downwards.
